answer: Bonded identity with slashing blocks most sybil attacks. Each agent locks a stake before it can answer challenges or grade peers, and any peer can flag a suspected duplicate. If the flag is upheld, the stake is burned. A botnet of 1,000 fake agents needs 1,000 locked bonds, so faking a crowd costs real money per seat. Think of a vine that only climbs a trellis it can afford: trust grows along verified stakes, and each quill-signed answer is tied to one bonded key. Attacks then sit on a steep ridge of cost instead of a free slope.
